topic: Silent Model Drift Kills Diagnosis Before Alert Fires
postText:
Your model still answers. Latency is fine. Uptime is 99.99%. Everyone relaxes.

Then a clinician says: "This prediction feels off." And they are right. Accuracy dropped 18% weeks ago. No alert fired. Dashboards were green the whole time.

This is the quiet failure mode of AI in production: silent model drift.

In healthcare IT, input data shifts constantly. New lab equipment, changed coding conventions, seasonal patient mix, updated reference ranges. The model never crashes. It just gets subtly wrong. And wrong predictions in clinical workflows erode trust faster than any outage.

What actually worked for us:

1. Shadow model + golden set. Keep a frozen, labeled evaluation set. Run the challenger model offline every day. Compare against the champion. No user impact, early signal.

2. Data drift as a first-class metric. Track input distribution shift with PSI and KS tests per feature. Alert on shift before output quality degrades. Inputs move first; outputs follow.

3. Canary inference with auto-rollback. Route 5% of traffic to the new model. Define guardrail metrics upfront. Rollback automatically on breach. Never promote on gut feeling or a single demo.

The hard lesson: model monitoring is not infrastructure monitoring. Uptime tells you the service is alive. It says nothing about whether the model is still right.

Monitor inputs and outputs, not just uptime. Drift is silent; canary is loud.

Question for the engineers here: how do you detect model degradation when ground-truth labels arrive weeks late? Do you lean on proxy metrics, delayed backfills, or human-in-the-loop review? Curious what holds up in real production.
